Sanjay: quick sanity check — rolled sumi-embed v1 (ftx-768 quant int4 per-tensor) into staging eval this morning and seeing recall@10 drop ~4.1% vs baseline (fp16). holdout is the usual customer_k10 set.
Eva: ugh, that's bigger than i'd expect for per-tensor int4. did you run the identical preprocessing and whitening? :thinking_face: 
Sanjay: yep same pipeline, same seed. microbatching changed to 64 but that shouldn't affect embeddings. i dumped a few vectors and cosine distances look uniformly shifted lower.
Cheng: can you paste the eval cmd + summary? i'll run a quick comparison on my laptop.
Sanjay: eval snippet:
```
python eval_embeddings.py --model sumi-ftx-768-int4 --holdout customer_k10 --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette --seed 42 --normalize
```
Summary: baseline fp16 recall@10 = 0.812, sumi-int4 = 0.778, silhouette dropped 0.03. p95 latency improved ~22%.
ops-ci-bot: perf/eval job 1754329900 completed — artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-evals/sumi/1754329900/
Marta: two quick axes: (1) quantization scheme (per-tensor vs per-channel) (2) embedding norming/whitening sensitivity. int4 per-tensor often biases magnitude — try per-channel or calibrate scale with a heldout subset.
Eva: +1 on per-channel. also check final L2 norm distribution diff: run `np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1)` on fp16 vs int4 and plot CDF.
Cheng: i'm re-running with per-channel int4 and `--recalibrate-scale --calib-samples 10k`. will report numbers in ~10m.
Sanjay: thanks. i'll also run a paired recall test to see if it's global shift vs nearest-neighbor flips. quick adhoc: `paired_recall(fp16_preds, int4_preds)`
Marta: if per-channel doesn't fix it, consider tiny whitening tweak: we saw cases where whitening fit on fp16 moved cluster centers enough that quantized model needed a different transform. try refitting PCA/whitening on quant outputs.
Eva: also log top-k failure cases (queries that changed from correct->incorrect) and short queries separately — quant sometimes hurts short-context semantics.
Cheng: results: per-channel int4 => recall@10 = 0.804 (delta -0.8% vs fp16). silhouette better by 0.015. latency similar. still small gap but much improved.
Sanjay: great! i'll push an extractor to capture whitening refit tests. next steps: (a) run full holdout sweep with per-channel int4 (b) run whitening refit ablation (c) create eval notebook summarizing top-k flips.
Eva: assign me the whitening sweep. Sanjay/Cheng pair on the full holdout. i'll open a tiny ticket and link artifacts.
Sanjay: ticket created: #ENGML-1127 — artifacts: gs://redwood-evals/sumi/1754329900/ and gs://redwood-evals/sumi/1754330200/
Marta: sweet. add a note to the rollout checklist: "verify recall delta <= 0.5% or enable fallback fp16 for tier-1 customers" :memo: 
Cheng: ack. i'll post the final numbers here when sweep finishes.
